summary.releaseRationale: Bundled OpenJPEG 2.5.4 is affected by OSV-2025-219 even though JP2/J2K is rejected by the current LocalDocForge media-type boundary. PDFium 152.0.7947.0 and all enumerated version-unknown nested children remain advisory-unknown. Empty exact-version database results are not treated as proof of safety, and the Windows-native inventory is compositionally incomplete for other target platforms.

verificationRuns.scope: Exact-version advisory refresh and isolated-build-backend provenance verification
verificationRuns.dataBoundary: Only public component names and exact public versions were submitted; no repository source, document data, filenames, environment values, credentials, or private paths were transmitted.

sources.conclusion: The official OSV batch API returned zero matching vulnerability records for the 29 exact PyPI name/version queries.
sources.disposition: The existing no-known-applicable-advisory records remain time-bounded no-findings, not safety guarantees.

sources.conclusion: The official OSV batch API returned one applicable match: OpenJPEG 2.5.4 maps to OSV-2025-219; no other exact native query returned a match.
sources.disposition: OpenJPEG remains affected; empty results remain time-bounded no-findings or unknown where provenance is insufficient.

sources.conclusion: The authoritative OSV record still enumerates v2.5.4 as affected by the HIGH-severity heap-buffer-overflow and identifies fixed commit d33cbecc148d3affcdf403211fddc2cc5d442379.

The exact Pillow tag retains its native OpenJPEG acquisition path; local exact-wheel notice evidence continues to identify bundled OpenJPEG 2.5.4, and no fixed same-version bundle evidence was established.

Official PyPI metadata authenticated the release wheel SHA-256 29b23c360f22f414dc7336bb39178cc7bcbf6021ed2733cde173f09dba19abb3 and sdist SHA-256 025bccbbf0fa05b6192bc64ae1e7b16e001fd6d6d4d5de03c97b1c1ade523bef used by the build-backend lock.
sources.disposition: approved as the hash-locked isolated PEP 517 build backend

verificationRuns.releaseRationale: The refresh did not remove the affected OpenJPEG result or resolve PDFium and unversioned-child provenance.

conclusionVocabulary.affected: An authoritative or official advisory source identifies the exact installed version as affected.
conclusionVocabulary.contains-affected-component: The component is an aggregate or distribution that contains an affected nested component.
conclusionVocabulary.contains-unknown-component: The component contains a nested component whose exact advisory disposition could not be established.
conclusionVocabulary.no-known-applicable-advisory: No advisory matching the exact version was identified in the named sources on the access date; this is not a safety guarantee.
conclusionVocabulary.unknown: Available provenance or advisory mapping is insufficient to reach an affected/not-affected conclusion.

authorityOrder: exact installed wheel license and notice files
moving upstream text only when exact source provenance is unavailable and the limitation is explicit
licenseVerification.exactVersionPolicy: A moving main/master license file alone is insufficient. Exact tag references are used wherever the upstream exposes a release tag; exact wheel/sdist evidence and a stated limitation are required otherwise.
licenseVerification.platformEvidence: Nested native versions and wheel notice bundles were inspected from Windows x86-64 / CPython 3.14 artifacts. Each other target platform requires equivalent wheel inventory and license retention.

unversionedComponentPolicy.licenseTreatment: Retain the complete aggregate wheel notice named by each record; no exact-version license conclusion is inferred when the child version is unavailable.
unversionedComponentPolicy.applicability: The child is physically represented by, linked into, or named in the inspected Windows wheel's native aggregate. Reachability follows its parent parser/codec.
unversionedComponentPolicy.remediation: Obtain an exact child version and source/build provenance, re-run authoritative license and advisory review, and rebuild or upgrade the parent wheel when provenance cannot be established.
unversionedComponentPolicy.residualRisk: Without an exact version or source revision, affected/not-affected status cannot be established; aggregate notice preservation does not resolve advisory provenance.

osv-oss-fuzz-exact.authority: official advisory database and OSS-Fuzz evidence

microsoft-vc-runtime-exact.authority: official Microsoft lifecycle, licensing, and Security Update Guide review
microsoft-vc-runtime-exact.limitation: Microsoft's public advisory portal does not provide a stable exact-DLL-version API mapping. No matching applicable advisory was identified on 2026-07-19; this is not proof of safety.

limitations: Database results are a time-bounded snapshot, not proof that a component has no vulnerability.
GitHub repository security tabs may omit vulnerabilities published only through OSS-Fuzz, vendor trackers, or private disclosure; OpenJPEG is a demonstrated example.

PDFium security bugs are generally handled through Chromium/Google private disclosure. The installed wheel records PDFium 152.0.7947.0 with n_commits=0 and hash=null, so public release notices cannot be mapped authoritatively to this binary.

The components array contains versioned review records, not an exhaustive native inventory. Known unversioned PDFium and Pillow/libavif children are enumerated separately, inherit unknown advisory provenance, and make the CycloneDX composition incomplete.

Native evidence comes from Windows x86-64 / CPython 3.14 wheels even though the Python lock and generated SBOM files are universal-profile artifacts. Other platform wheels require independent native inventory.
Platform markers mean a package can be absent on a particular operating system. Dispositions apply whenever the listed artifact is installed.

components.name: annotated-doc
components.role: Annotation documentation helper used transitively by Typer and FastAPI; document bytes are not passed to it.

security.applicability: No direct untrusted-document or HTTP parsing path was identified.
security.remediation: Keep the hash lock and repeat exact-version review on upgrade.
security.residualRisk: Unpublished issues and supply-chain compromise remain possible; no-finding is not a safety claim.

components.name: annotated-types
components.role: Constraint metadata consumed by Pydantic.

security.applicability: Only application-declared type metadata is consumed; untrusted files do not define annotations.
security.remediation: Keep the hash lock and repeat exact-version review on upgrade.
security.residualRisk: Pydantic behavior still depends on this metadata; unpublished semantic-validation defects remain possible.

components.name: anyio
components.role: ASGI concurrency layer used by Starlette when the local web service is enabled.

security.applicability: Reachable indirectly through concurrent API requests only in standard/full profiles; the service defaults to loopback.
security.remediation: Retain request, concurrency, timeout, and process-isolation controls and update if a matching advisory appears.
security.residualRisk: Concurrency cancellation and resource-exhaustion defects can still affect availability even without a published advisory.

components.name: click
components.role: Command-line parsing dependency of Uvicorn.

security.applicability: Parses trusted local launch arguments; uploaded document bytes are not passed to Click.
security.remediation: Keep the hash lock and repeat exact-version review on upgrade.
security.residualRisk: Terminal and argument-handling defects remain possible for attacker-influenced filenames shown by higher layers.

components.name: colorama
components.role: Windows terminal-color compatibility for CLI output.

security.applicability: Used only on Windows for local terminal output; it does not parse document bodies.
security.remediation: Keep output escaping/bounds in higher layers and repeat review on upgrade.
security.residualRisk: Unpublished terminal-control handling defects remain possible.

components.name: fastapi
components.role: Local HTTP API routing, request validation, and response serialization.

security.applicability: Directly reachable by untrusted HTTP requests when `ldf web` is running; loopback is the default but nonlocal mode exists outside strict-offline mode.
security.remediation: Maintain token/Host/body/field controls and promptly update on any matching framework advisory.
security.residualRisk: Framework logic and dependency interactions may expose unpublished request-smuggling, validation, or denial-of-service issues.

components.name: h11
components.role: HTTP/1.1 protocol parser used by Uvicorn.

security.applicability: Attacker-controlled HTTP bytes reach h11 whenever the standard/full web server is enabled.
security.remediation: Keep Uvicorn/h11 jointly current and preserve request-size, timeout, concurrency, and loopback controls.
security.residualRisk: Protocol differential and request-smuggling defects may arise from interactions with Uvicorn or intermediaries.

components.name: idna
components.role: Internationalized-domain helper pulled by AnyIO; LocalDocForge ships no outbound client.

security.applicability: No application route passes untrusted document domains to IDNA; it is retained by the ASGI dependency closure.
security.remediation: Keep the hash lock and remove the dependency if the upstream closure no longer requires it.
security.residualRisk: Future API or networking features could make normalization issues reachable.

components.name: lxml
components.role: Native XML library used by pikepdf, including document metadata paths.

security.applicability: Malformed PDF XML/XMP metadata may reach native XML code through pikepdf; external-entity/network behavior is not intentionally invoked.
security.remediation: Keep lxml and its exact wheel current, reject malformed PDFs, and retain worker/resource containment.
security.residualRisk: The wheel contains native XML code whose lower-level library revisions are not separate records in this SBOM.

components.name: markdown-it-py
components.role: Rich Markdown rendering dependency for local CLI presentation; Markdown document conversion is not enabled.

security.applicability: User documents are not parsed as Markdown; only application-controlled CLI presentation uses this dependency.
security.remediation: Keep the hash lock and repeat review before enabling Markdown conversion.
security.residualRisk: Future rendering of attacker-controlled Markdown would materially change reachability.

components.name: mdurl
components.role: URL parser used by markdown-it-py; document Markdown conversion is disabled.

security.applicability: No untrusted document URL is routed to mdurl in current capabilities.
security.remediation: Preserve both MIT notices and repeat review before enabling Markdown input.
security.residualRisk: URL normalization issues become relevant if attacker-controlled Markdown is later enabled.

components.name: packaging
components.role: Version and requirement parsing dependency of pikepdf.

security.applicability: Only trusted installed-package metadata and application constraints are parsed.
security.remediation: Preserve the chosen dual-license terms and repeat exact-version review on upgrade.
security.residualRisk: Malformed local package metadata could still trigger parser defects.

components.name: pikepdf
components.role: Primary structural PDF wrapper; untrusted PDFs are opened through bundled qpdf.

security.applicability: Directly processes attacker-controlled PDFs; wrapper defects and bundled qpdf behavior are both relevant.
security.remediation: Keep pikepdf/qpdf current as a pair, reject parser warnings, and retain hard worker/resource isolation.
security.residualRisk: No exact-version advisory was found, but native parser memory-safety and denial-of-service defects may be unpublished.

components.name: pillow
components.role: Primary image decoder/encoder and owner of the bundled native codec set.

affectedVersionRanges: OpenJPEG versions v2.*, v2.5.3, and v2.5.4 as enumerated by OSV-2025-219
security.applicability: Allowed JPEG/PNG/TIFF/BMP/WebP inputs reach Pillow. JP2/J2K is not recognized by sniff.py and is excluded from images-to-PDF accepted types, so the affected OpenJPEG codec is bundled but not directly reachable through declared formats.
security.remediation: Use a Pillow wheel whose OpenJPEG includes upstream fix d33cbecc148d3affcdf403211fddc2cc5d442379 or a later fixed release; until then preserve JP2/J2K rejection and hard worker/resource isolation.
security.residualRisk: Format confusion, plugin changes, or future JPEG2000 enablement could expose the affected codec; other native codecs still process hostile bytes.

components.name: pydantic
components.role: Domain, configuration, report, and API parameter validation.

security.applicability: Attacker-controlled API form parameters and local CLI values reach application Pydantic models; raw document bodies do not.
security.remediation: Keep Pydantic and pydantic-core aligned and retain explicit application bounds.
security.residualRisk: Validation bypass or algorithmic-complexity defects can exist without a published advisory.

components.name: pydantic_core
components.role: Native Rust validation engine used by Pydantic.

license.exactVersionEvidence: pydantic 2.13.4 pins pydantic-core 2.46.4; the installed pydantic_core-2.46.4.dist-info/licenses/LICENSE matches the tag-pinned text

security.applicability: Attacker-controlled API parameters reach native validation code under application schemas.
security.remediation: Update only with a compatible Pydantic release and retain explicit size/range limits before expensive validation.
security.residualRisk: The Rust extension is native code and is not a sandbox; unpublished panics or resource-exhaustion defects remain possible.

components.name: pydantic-settings
components.role: Loads LocalDocForge configuration from trusted local environment and dotenv sources.

security.applicability: Requires attacker influence over the process environment or local configuration files, outside the untrusted-document boundary.
security.remediation: Protect local configuration permissions and repeat review on upgrade.
security.residualRisk: A same-user local attacker can already influence broader application state; this package is not a trust boundary.

components.name: Pygments
components.role: Syntax-highlighting dependency of Rich; document text is not highlighted by current capabilities.

security.applicability: No current path sends extracted document text or source code to Pygments.
security.remediation: Remove if Rich no longer needs it or repeat review before highlighting untrusted content.
security.residualRisk: Lexer complexity becomes relevant if attacker-controlled highlighting is later introduced.

components.name: pypdf
components.role: Full-profile diagnostic import only; production operations are not permitted to fall back to pypdf.

security.applicability: The exact package is import-probed but untrusted PDFs are not passed to it in supported production operations.
security.remediation: Keep it confined to the full diagnostic profile and re-review before enabling any parser fallback.
security.residualRisk: Reachability would change immediately if a future fallback or operation opens documents with pypdf.

components.name: pypdfium2

license.concluded: Apache-2.0 OR BSD-3-Clause; documentation/examples CC-BY-4.0; bundled dependency licenses apply
license.exactVersionEvidence: installed pypdfium2-5.12.1.dist-info/licenses contains Apache-2.0, BSD-3-Clause, CC-BY-4.0, and platform BUILD_LICENSES texts

security.applicability: Every PDF candidate rendered for validation and every PDF-to-image input reaches the bundled PDFium binary.
security.remediation: Require pypdfium2/pdfium-binaries to publish an exact PDFium source commit, map it to Chromium/PDFium fixes, and rebuild/update from a vetted revision.

components.name: python-dotenv

components.name: python-multipart

components.name: rich

components.name: shellingham

components.name: starlette

security.residualRisk: Historical advisories show upload/request parsing is security-sensitive; no exact match does not eliminate new defects.

components.name: typer

components.name: typing_extensions

security.applicability: Provides application/framework type objects; it does not parse documents or requests.
security.remediation: Keep the hash lock and repeat exact-version review on upgrade.

components.name: typing-inspection
components.role: Type-introspection helper used by Pydantic/FastAPI.

security.applicability: Inspects application-defined types rather than attacker-defined code.
security.remediation: Keep aligned with Pydantic/FastAPI and repeat review on upgrade.
security.residualRisk: Semantic introspection defects may cause validation differences without constituting a published vulnerability.

components.name: uvicorn
components.role: ASGI server for `ldf web`.

security.applicability: Directly accepts untrusted socket/HTTP traffic when standard/full web mode is running; loopback is the default.
security.remediation: Keep Uvicorn and h11 jointly current and preserve loopback default, Host/token controls, and admission/resource limits.
security.residualRisk: Protocol handling, disconnect, and resource-exhaustion defects may be unpublished or interaction-specific.

components.name: libwebp

components.name: openjpeg
components.role: Native JPEG2000 codec bundled by Pillow; JP2/J2K is rejected by current LocalDocForge media gates.

advisories.provenanceConclusion: The Pillow 12.3.0 tag selects OpenJPEG 2.5.4; the Windows build downloads the exact upstream v2.5.4 archive and declares no OpenJPEG patch. No checksum evidence establishes that a same-version pillow-depends archive is patched, so it is not credited as remediated.

affectedVersionRanges: GIT 954c6e3cb9d79aaa08c6666373d2bfa04f89ead1 to before d33cbecc148d3affcdf403211fddc2cc5d442379; OSV enumerates v2.5.4 as affected
security.applicability: The exact Windows-wheel nested component is affected. Direct exploitability currently requires reaching JPEG2000 decode, but sniff.py and images-to-PDF reject JP2/J2K; PDF JPEG2000 rendering uses PDFium rather than Pillow's OpenJPEG. Other target-platform wheels require equivalent native provenance review.
security.remediation: Replace the Pillow native build with one containing fix d33cbecc148d3affcdf403211fddc2cc5d442379 or a later fixed OpenJPEG release; keep JP2/J2K rejected and retain hard worker/resource isolation meanwhile.
security.residualRisk: An allowlist bypass, plugin behavior change, or future JPEG2000 support would make hostile decoding reachable.

components.name: PDFium
components.role: Native PDF renderer used for candidate validation and PDF-to-image conversion.

license.localVersionEvidence: pypdfium2_raw/version.json: 152.0.7947.0, origin=pdfium-binaries, n_commits=0, hash=null; wheel BUILD_LICENSES/pdfium.txt and related files
license.upstreamTextLimitation: No exact PDFium source revision is recorded by the wheel, so the moving upstream license URL is paired with the exact wheel's bundled license texts; this does not resolve security provenance

security.applicability: Directly parses and renders every untrusted PDF candidate/input. Chromium/PDFium security reports may remain private until fixes ship.
security.remediation: Obtain the exact source commit/build provenance from pdfium-binaries, map it to Chromium/PDFium security fixes, and rebuild or upgrade from a vetted revision.
security.residualRisk: No source hash is recorded and public branch/build numbering does not establish which private security fixes are present; do not treat this component as safe.

components.name: Microsoft Visual C++ Runtime (msvcp140.dll)
components.role: C++ standard-library runtime DLL physically bundled beside qpdf in the inspected pikepdf Windows wheel.

license.concluded: Microsoft Visual C++ Runtime 2015-2022 Software License Terms
license.localVersionEvidence: pikepdf.libs/msvcp140-0f885b509a685d2bbfa652fed26b5fb3.dll; FileVersion=14.44.35211.0; 557728 bytes; SHA256=0f885b509a685d2bbfa652fed26b5fb31d88fbdab0a978c641d1c7b8aa460aa9; pikepdf-10.10.0.dist-info/licenses/licenses-for-wheels.txt preserves Microsoft distributable-code terms
license.vendorLifecycleEvidence: Microsoft identifies runtime 14.44.35211 with Visual Studio 2022 v17.14 final and support through 2032-01-13

security.remediation: Ship the latest supported compatible pikepdf wheel/runtime, retain Microsoft's distributable-code terms, and repeat the Microsoft advisory review when the DLL changes.

components.name: Pillow codec bundle
components.role: Aggregate SBOM record for the native libraries shipped in the inspected Pillow wheel.

license.concluded: Multiple licenses; child-component terms and the complete Pillow wheel license bundle apply

affectedVersionRanges: OpenJPEG v2.5.4 is enumerated as affected by OSV-2025-219
security.applicability: JPEG, PNG, TIFF, BMP, and WebP paths reach selected native children; JP2/J2K and AVIF/HEIF remain rejected by the current operation allowlist.

components.name: qpdf
components.role: Native structural PDF parser/rewriter used through pikepdf.

security.applicability: Untrusted PDFs directly reach qpdf through pikepdf for inspection and structural operations.
security.remediation: Keep pikepdf/qpdf current together, reject parser warnings, and retain hard worker/resource isolation.
security.residualRisk: Native parser memory, CPU, and correctness defects can be unpublished; no exact-match result is not a safety verdict.

components.name: tiff

security.remediation: Keep libtiff/Pillow current and enforce frame, pixel, decompression, disk, timeout, and worker limits.

components.name: xz

security.remediation: Keep exact wheel provenance and hashes, monitor upstream releases, and remove unused codec support in custom builds where practical.
security.residualRisk: Historical XZ supply-chain compromise makes artifact provenance and hash verification essential even at an unaffected version.

components.name: zlib-ng
